newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Greenfields changes capital raising plans.
newsitem.headline: Greenfields changes capital raising plans.

text.p: Greenfields Coal Co Ltd said on Thursday it planned a capital reconstruction and options issue to shareholders to help it proceed to full production of a coal recovery plant in the United States.
The company, which operates the Alpheus plant in West Virginia, said it would halve its issued ordinary capital and then issue about A$10 million of 20 cent ordinary shares.
It also said it would offer shareholders one free option to buy one ordinary share at 20 cents each.
Greenfields shares ended 2.5 cents higher at 16 cents.
The company said it was discussing the underwriting and pre-sale of some of the new shares with stockbrokers.
It said the capital reconstruction and fall in the share price below 20 cents meant that it would not proceed with a one-for-four rights issue announced on June 4.
Funds raised would be used to retire debt and for working capital to move to full production of the plant.
The company said it would have annual output of 240,000 tons of clean coal from the plant once full production was achieved, with the coal to be bought by US Steel at US$21 per ton.
